categoryName: Women health & hygiene — sanitary pads, tampons, menstrual cups, intimate wash, pregnancy tests

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — ultra-thin regular/L, mass brand
skuLines.examples: Whisper Ultra Clean L, Stayfree Secure Dry Cottony, Sofy Antibacterial Regular, Niine Dry Comfort Ultra Thin
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, but campus-wide demand collapses in school vacation months (Jun, late Dec-Jan) when residents leave; restock ahead of session re-open
skuLines.marginBand: 10-18% (est.; national brands run thin trade margins, modern-trade slabs reach ~20%)
skuLines.notes: THE anchor SKU of the whole category — never allow a stockout, 30-50 km of hill road means a gap sends a wallet off-campus. Bulky and low-density: a carton is cube-limited not weight-limited, so freight per unit is high — order in full cases. Shelf life 2-3 yrs but fluff pulp absorbs monsoon humidity: store palletised off the floor, away from outer walls. Nil GST (HSN 9619).

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — XL/XXL night, mass brand
skuLines.examples: Whisper Bindazzz Night XL+, Stayfree Dry Max All Night, Sofy Side Walls Extra Long, Niine Ultra Thin XL+
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; heavier pull in a residential hostel where girls sleep 8-9 hrs in shared rooms and cannot change at night
skuLines.notes: In a boarding-school setting night pads matter more than in a home market — this is the line that prevents bed/linen accidents. Stock at least 2 night SKUs (one mass, one XXXL). Nil GST.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — XXXL / extra-long overnight, premium claim
skuLines.examples: Whisper Bindazzz Night XXXL, Carmesi Air Feel Night XXXL+ 16s, Sofy Overnight 42cm, Everteen XXXL 40s
skuLines.priceBand: ₹120-350 depending on count (Carmesi 16 XXXL+ = ₹329 at brand MRP)
skuLines.notes: Size inflation is the main premiumisation lever in Indian femcare right now — 'XXXL' and breathable/air-flow backsheets are the claim being sold. One facing is enough; it trades slowly but at 2-3x the ticket.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — cottony / soft-top sensitive-skin variant
skuLines.examples: Stayfree Secure Cottony Soft, Sofy Cool Cotton, Niine Naturally Soft, Whisper Choice Cotton
skuLines.seasonality: Rash complaints spike in the heavy monsoon (Jul-Sep) when nothing dries — cottony/breathable variants pull hardest then
skuLines.notes: Adolescent boarders in humid hill monsoon get pad rash; a soft-top option is a genuine medical-comfort SKU, not a marketing tier. Same nil-GST, same humidity storage caution.

skuLines.examples: Whisper Choice, Stayfree Secure (non-ultra), Bella Rio Regular, Anandi
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; strongest around salary dates for non-teaching staff households
skuLines.notes: Non-teaching staff and older women buy on price per pad, not on brand or thinness. If only premium is on shelf, this cohort simply reverts to cloth — a real hygiene outcome, not just a lost sale.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — value regional brand, high-count economy pack
skuLines.examples: Bella Rio 40s, Niine 30s value pack, Sakhi / Suvidha (Jan Aushadhi), Aisha
skuLines.marginBand: 20-35% (est.; regional brands buy shelf space with margin)
skuLines.notes: The cheap end is where a captive-market store earns trust. Nil GST means the whole ₹1-vs-₹7 per-pad spread is positioning and margin, not tax — so a value line can be priced kindly and still make more money than the national brand.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — jumbo/family pack 40-50s (household + hostel stock-up)
skuLines.examples: Whisper Ultra 50s, Stayfree 42s combo, Everteen XXL 40s (₹219), Sofy 40s
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes right before long vacations and before monsoon road closures
skuLines.notes: Purpose-built for exactly this geography: a resident 30-50 km from a market buys 2-3 months at once. Best cash-per-facing in the whole category. Watch pack integrity — big packs sit longest and swell in damp.

skuLines.examples: Saathi Bamboo Fiber 12s, Niine Bio, Carmesi (compostable wrap), Pee Safe Biodegradable Overnight 10s (₹219)
skuLines.notes: Real strategic value here is disposal, not eco-credentials: a closed township has to burn or bury everything it consumes, so a compostable pad reduces the campus's own incinerator load. Keep it to one SKU until it proves out — 2-3x price is a hard sell to students on pocket money.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad — organic-cotton top sheet, rash-free premium
skuLines.examples: Nua, Carmesi Sensitive, Sofy Organic Cotton, Rio Organic
skuLines.notes: Buyer here is the faculty/university-student end, not the school. One SKU, one facing. D2C brands rarely have hill distribution — expect to source through a modern-trade distributor or direct, with MOQ pain.

skuLines.examples: Whisper Choice Regular (small), Sofy Bodyfit small, Niine Regular 6s, teen-format pads in 6s
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes at academic session start (Jul) as new boarders arrive
skuLines.notes: Non-obvious but critical for this store: Akal Academy boards girls from age 5, so first periods (menarche ~10-13) happen on campus, away from mothers. A small-body pad in a low-cost 6s pack is the SKU a 11-year-old and her warden can actually buy. Pair with the menarche kit line.

skuLines.examples: Everteen Daily Panty Liners (₹129), Pee Safe Aloe Vera 20s/50s (₹179 for 50), Carefree, Whisper Daily Liners
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon — daily discharge and dampness complaints rise Jul-Sep
skuLines.notes: 17.6% of the Indian femcare market by value (IMARC) — the second-biggest segment after pads and usually the biggest gap in a small-town store's range. Compact and light: cheap to freight up the hill, unlike pads.

skuLines.examples: Saathi Bamboo Panty Liner (from ₹240), Carmesi Panty Liners, Sirona long liners, everteen long liners
skuLines.notes: Single facing. Low weight, long shelf life — a safe line to overstock relative to pads.

skuLines.examples: Sirona applicator-free tampons, Pee Safe tampons, Lemme Be, Sofy tampons
skuLines.notes: Honest read: tampons are the fastest-growing Indian segment (~13.9% share, ~16.5% CAGR per IMARC) but that growth is metro and English-media driven. On a conservative Sikh institutional campus with school-age boarders, insertable products face real cultural resistance. Stock ONE tampon SKU as a service line for university students and visiting faculty — do not build depth on the national trend.

skuLines.examples: Sirona applicator tampons, Tampax (import), Carefree applicator
skuLines.notes: Only if the non-applicator line moves. Applicators are what first-time users can actually manage, so if you carry exactly one tampon SKU, arguably it should be this one.

skuLines.examples: Pee Safe Menstrual Cup S/M/L (₹289 each), Sirona, Saathi Reusable Cup (₹499), Everteen cup, Asan
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; best sold at session start when a student is deciding her year's routine
skuLines.notes: Economically this is the single best product for a captive hill population — one ₹300-500 cup replaces ~10 years of pads that have to be trucked 50 km up and then burned on campus. But it needs boiling water, a private washroom and counselling to adopt; in shared hostel bathrooms that is a genuine barrier. Sell it with the sterilizer and a demo, or it dies on the shelf. Size guidance matters (S for unmarried/no vaginal birth).

skuLines.line: Menstrual cup starter kit + sterilizer container / sterilising tablets
skuLines.examples: Pee Safe Cup (M) + Sterilizer Container (₹399), Saathi Sterilizer Container (₹249), Sirona cup kit, Milton-type tablets
skuLines.notes: The bundle, not the bare cup, is what converts a first-time user in a hostel — a microwave/kettle-safe container removes the 'boil it in the shared kitchen' problem. Cup lifespan ~10 yrs, so a repeat sale never comes: all the money is in the first kit and the consumable wash.

skuLines.examples: Azah Anti-Microbial Menstrual Cup Wash (₹179), Sirona cup wash, Pee Safe cup wash
skuLines.notes: The only recurring revenue a cup customer generates. Tiny, light, long shelf life. Pointless without cup sales — attach it, don't range it standalone.

skuLines.examples: Imported/D2C discs (Sirona, niche brands)
skuLines.notes: Newest premium format; wider and sits higher than a bell cup, slightly higher capacity. Almost certainly too early for this catchment — listed for completeness of the ideal assortment, would be my first cut.

skuLines.line: Reusable cloth pad — single / twin pack
skuLines.examples: Eco Femme Super Comfy Twin Pack (₹710), Eco Femme Night Pad Twin (₹610), Boondh, Pee Safe Reusable Pads (3 regular + 1 night, ₹339)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; hardest sell in monsoon when nothing dries
skuLines.notes: Genuinely well-matched to a closed township: no disposal burden, no repeat freight. The killer constraint is local — Rajgarh's heavy monsoon and cold means cloth pads may not sun-dry for days, which is exactly the hygiene failure mode. Pitch as a backup/economy tier alongside disposables, never as a replacement, and pair with a covered drying line.

skuLines.examples: Eco Femme Full Cycle Kit (₹1,825-1,905), Eco Femme Heavy Flow Kit of 4 (₹1,120), Boondh kit
skuLines.notes: ₹1,100+ ticket is a hard ask on a campus wage. This is the natural SKU for a Trust-funded / subsidised issue programme to school girls rather than a walk-in retail line — see adjacent services.

skuLines.examples: Azah Disposable Period Panty 4s (₹169) & 10s (₹399), Azah Teen Panty 5s (₹199), Everteen Disposable Period Panties (₹169), Carmesi
skuLines.packSizes: Box of 4, 5, 10; size bands M-L / L-XL / XL-XXL
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at heavy-flow nights, travel home, sports/exam days
skuLines.notes: The clear breakout format of 2025-26 — every D2C brand I checked (Azah, Everteen, Carmesi) now leads its range with it, and Azah even runs a dedicated TEEN size. Ideal for a boarding school: no belt, no shifting, nothing to change at 2am, and it is a modest, fully-covered product a warden can hand out. Strong candidate to overweight versus the market.

skuLines.examples: Adira, Sochgreen, Lemme Be, Nykd by Nykaa period panty
skuLines.notes: Sizing depth kills small stores — six sizes x styles is a lot of dead stock at ₹700 each. If carried, put it in the CLOTHING store (where sizing and a trial process already exist) rather than the POS store, and keep to 2 sizes of one style.

skuLines.examples: VWash Plus (Glenmark), Everteen Natural Intimate Wash, Clean & Dry, Pee Safe Women's Intimate Wash 105 ml (₹126)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong monsoon skew (Jul-Sep) — humidity, damp clothing and shared bathrooms drive itching/discharge complaints
skuLines.notes: 'Spray and internal cleansers' are ~9.4% of the Indian market (IMARC) and this is the highest-value-per-cubic-foot line in the whole category — light, non-fragile, 2-3 yr shelf life, cheap to haul up the hill. In a township where 5,000 people share limited bathrooms, this is a must-have, not a beauty product. Attracts full GST (unlike pads).

skuLines.examples: Himalaya intimate wash, Namyaa, Sirona, everteen Neem-Tulsi
skuLines.notes: Herbal framing sells far better than clinical framing to older and more traditional buyers — matters in this catchment. Same logistics as above.

skuLines.examples: VWash sachets, Everteen small pack, 20-30 ml travel packs
skuLines.notes: The single best trial mechanic for a student with pocket money and no privacy — a ₹10-20 sachet is buyable without a conversation. Also the format that converts first-time users into 100 ml buyers. Frequently missing from small-store ranges.

skuLines.examples: Pee Safe Natural Intimate Wipes 10s (₹59), Everteen wipes, Sirona wipes, Carmesi
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks on travel/vacation departure dates and in monsoon
skuLines.notes: Made for exactly this situation — a 30-50 km bus ride on hill road with no clean toilet. Also a hostel-bathroom substitute. Cheap ticket, high impulse, tiny cube. Warn on disposal: 'flushable' wipes wreck small-township septic/STP lines, so sell with a disposal bag.

skuLines.examples: Pee Safe Toilet Seat Sanitizer Mint 75 ml (₹180), Carmesi toilet seat sanitizer, Sirona
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at session start and before school trips
skuLines.notes: In a township where thousands share hostel and block toilets this is one of the highest-relevance SKUs in my lane, and the one most likely to be absent. Pocket 25 ml is the student SKU; 75 ml the family one. Aerosol/alcohol content — check transport rules on the carrier hauling it up the ghat.

skuLines.line: Intimate anti-rash / anti-chafing cream & feminine powder
skuLines.examples: Sirona anti-chafing rash cream, Namyaa intimate cream, Nycil/Dermi Cool prickly-heat powder used for the purpose
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp monsoon spike (Jul-Sep) and again in any warm spell — pad rash and thigh chafing
skuLines.notes: A boarding population in a humid monsoon with limited laundry turnaround gets pad rash constantly, and the current answer is usually nothing. Cheap, small, high-repeat. Keep to cosmetic/ayurvedic claims — a medicated antifungal is a drug-licence item (below).

skuLines.examples: Sirona Cramp Comfort heat patches, Nua Cramp Comfort, generic 12-hr menstrual heat patches
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, with a clear winter lift (Nov-Feb) — cold hill weather worsens cramping and heat is the first thing anyone reaches for
skuLines.notes: Cramp relief became a real sub-category in 2025-26 rather than an accessory. For a residential school this is the SKU that keeps a girl in class instead of in the sick room — worth stocking properly. Air-activated: sealed packs, check the expiry, humidity degrades them.

skuLines.examples: Pee Safe Cramp Relief Roll On 10 ml (₹169), Sirona roll-on, Carmesi BREASE 10 ml (₹299)
skuLines.notes: Non-drug, so no licence — makes it the pain SKU a school store can sell freely to a 15-year-old when a tablet needs the dispensary. That is a real advantage in this setting.

skuLines.line: Hot water bottle / electric heating pad
skuLines.examples: Duckback/Flamingo rubber hot water bottle, Dr Physio electric heating pad, gel hot-cold pack
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy winter (Nov-Feb) — doubles as cold-weather comfort in an unheated hill hostel
skuLines.notes: Sells for two reasons at once here: cramps and a cold Himachal winter — so it clears at full price Nov-Feb and needs almost no femcare framing. Bulky but non-perishable; buy once a year, pre-monsoon, ahead of the season.

skuLines.examples: Meftal Spas, Cyclopam, generic paracetamol, Combiflam
skuLines.notes: CONSTRAINT, read before ranging: these are Schedule H drugs — selling them needs a retail drug licence (Form 20/21) and a registered pharmacist, and mefenamic acid carries a DCGI adverse-reaction warning. For a campus with 5-18 year-old boarders the right home for this is the campus dispensary, not the POS counter. Listed because the ideal assortment includes it — flagged because ARY probably should not be the one selling it.

skuLines.examples: Gynoveda Iron Folic Acid Tablets (₹469), Autrin, Dexorange syrup, Fefol
skuLines.notes: Adolescent-girl anaemia in Himachal is very high and heavy periods make it worse — arguably the highest health-impact line in my lane. Drug-licence question depends on the SKU: an FSSAI nutraceutical iron tablet can be sold on a food licence, a pharma iron-folic brand cannot. Range the nutraceutical version and leave the pharma one to the dispensary.

skuLines.examples: Neurobion/Shelcal-type calcium, HealthKart HK Vitals women's multivitamin, Himalaya women's wellness
skuLines.seasonality: Winter lift (low sun, indoor months) for vitamin D
skuLines.notes: Nutraceutical, FSSAI not drug licence — cleanly sellable. Real relevance for staff women and elderly residents in a cold, low-sunlight hill location. Watch expiry: slow-moving, 18-24 month shelf life.

skuLines.line: Cycle-regulation / PCOS ayurvedic or myo-inositol course
skuLines.examples: Gynoveda PCOS-PCOD regimens (₹1,875-2,250), Gynoveda Delayed Cycle (₹1,313), myo-inositol sachets, Himalaya Menosan
skuLines.notes: Went mainstream in 2025-26. High ticket, slow rotation, and needs a conversation nobody wants to have at a busy counter — the honest recommendation is order-on-request via the discreet WhatsApp channel rather than shelf stock. Confidence that this sells at ARY: low.

skuLines.examples: Gynoveda Smooth Menopause Transition (₹1,875), Gynoveda White Discharge & Itching (₹1,313), Himalaya Menosan
skuLines.notes: Named because the resident base explicitly includes elderly and long-serving staff women, a cohort femcare ranges usually forget entirely. Order-on-request, not shelf stock.

skuLines.examples: Sirona UTI/cranberry sachets, HealthKart cranberry, Cystolite-type sachets, Gynocure
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon and winter — less water drunk in cold weather plus shared toilets means UTIs cluster
skuLines.notes: Non-drug supplement version is freely sellable; alkalising urinary sachets (Cital/Alkasol) are drug-licence items. UTI is one of the most common reasons a woman here would otherwise make a 50 km trip to a doctor — worth carrying the OTC support tier.

skuLines.examples: Clotrimazole (Candid), Canesten, medicated intimate creams
skuLines.notes: CONSTRAINT: drug, retail drug licence + pharmacist required. Monsoon in a damp hill hostel makes fungal infection genuinely common, so the demand is real — but this belongs to the campus dispensary. Include it in the ideal list, route the sale correctly.

skuLines.examples: Prega News, i-can (Piramal), Velocit, Dr Morepen PregaScreen
skuLines.notes: Married staff families are explicitly part of this population and the nearest chemist is 30-50 km away, so this is a genuine must-have — the alternative is a day's travel or nothing. Handle with care: an IVD medical device (Medical Devices Rules 2017) so a retail sale licence may be required depending on the HP drug controller's reading; and in a small closed township it must be sold with real discretion — opaque bag, no comment, ideally not at the busiest counter. 18-24 month shelf life, temperature-sensitive: do not store near a heater or in direct sun.

skuLines.line: Pregnancy test kit — multipack / midstream / digital
skuLines.examples: Azah Basic Pregnancy Test Kit pack of 3 (₹179), Prega News 2-pack, i-can 3-pack, Clearblue digital (premium)
skuLines.notes: A multipack is the better SKU for a remote location — a test is usually repeated after a few days and nobody wants a second 50 km trip. Same licence and discretion notes as above.

skuLines.examples: i-know (Piramal), Prega News Ovulation, LH strip kits
skuLines.notes: For married staff couples trying to conceive — a quietly important, entirely unserved need in a closed community. Low volume, high discretion, order-on-request is fine. Same IVD licence question as pregnancy tests.

skuLines.examples: NewMom Maternity Sanitary Pads (₹188-204), Mee Mee maternity pads, Newmom Pad Fixator (₹221)
skuLines.notes: Directly targets 'married staff families with small children and babies'. Longer, wider and far more absorbent than a period pad — an ordinary XXL is not a substitute, which is why its absence forces a trip to town at the worst possible moment for a new mother. Low unit volume, near-zero substitution, so a small permanent facing is the right call. Nil GST (HSN 9619).

skuLines.examples: NewMom nursing pads, Mee Mee disposable nursing pads, Johnson's, Chicco
skuLines.notes: High-frequency consumable for every breastfeeding mother on campus — used daily for months, which makes it a far better repeat line than maternity pads. Light and compressible, easy freight.

skuLines.examples: Lanolin nipple cream (Mee Mee, Chicco), Carmesi BREASE roll-on (₹299), Bio-Oil for stretch marks
skuLines.seasonality: Winter — cold, dry hill air makes cracking worse
skuLines.notes: Small attach-on to the nursing-pad line, single facing. Genuinely relieves a painful early-breastfeeding problem that has no local alternative.

skuLines.line: Sanitary pad disposal bags / opaque disposal pouches
skuLines.examples: Sirona disposal bags, Pee Safe disposal bags, generic scented opaque pouches, paper disposal covers
skuLines.notes: Underrated in exactly this setting: a closed township handles its own waste, hostel bathrooms are shared, and modesty norms make visible disposal a real distress point. Cheap, tiny, high-margin, near-zero freight — and it makes the whole category easier for a shy 12-year-old to use. Pairs with the incinerator programme below.

skuLines.line: Institutional bulk carton — top-selling mass pad, case rate
skuLines.examples: Case packs of Whisper/Stayfree/Niine 20s-30s bought by hostel wardens and the Academy stores dept
skuLines.seasonality: Ordered against the academic calendar, not the retail month — lands before Jul session start and after winter break
skuLines.notes: This is where the real volume in the category sits at a residential institution: the hostels and the Academy buy in cases for warden-issue and emergency stock, not girl-by-girl at the POS. Thin percentage, huge absolute cash, and it dramatically improves your buying power on the retail SKUs. Warehouse the cases, not the POS store — and keep them off the floor through monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Assembled in-house: 6 small pads + 6 night pads + disposal bags + intimate wipes + a simple Punjabi/Hindi leaflet + a pouch; or Nua/Carmesi first-period kits
skuLines.seasonality: Concentrated at session start (Jul) and rolling through the year as girls reach menarche
skuLines.notes: The highest-impact single idea in this lane for this specific store. Akal Academy boards girls from age 5, so hundreds of first periods happen on campus with no mother present. A pre-made discreet kit a warden or the school nurse can hand over in one motion removes the need for an 11-year-old to ask a shopkeeper for anything. Assemble it from lines you already stock — no new sourcing, better margin than the components, and it is the kind of programme a Trust will fund.

skuLines.line: Light-bladder-leakage liners / adult incontinence pads for women
skuLines.examples: Friends Active/Ultrathinz LBL pads, Depend/Kotex-type liners, Nobel Hygiene Friends pads
skuLines.seasonality: Winter lift (cold increases urgency); year-round base
skuLines.notes: Elderly residents are named in the population and post-childbirth staff women need it too, yet LBL is the most commonly missing line in any small store — the workaround is a sanitary pad, which is the wrong absorbency and causes rash. High dignity value, no substitute available within 50 km. Bulky like pads, same humidity storage rules.

trends2026: Disposable period panties are the breakout format of 2025-26 — every Indian D2C femcare brand now leads its range with them (Azah 4s ₹169 / 10s ₹399, Everteen ₹169, Carmesi), and Azah has launched a dedicated TEEN size, which makes this the single most relevant new format for a boarding-school catchment.

Tampons are the fastest-growing segment of the Indian market (~13.9% share, ~16.5% CAGR per IMARC) off a small base — but the growth is metro/English-media led, so on a conservative institutional campus it is a one-SKU service line, not a bet.

Size inflation is the main premiumisation lever: XXXL / 'air-flow' / breathable-backsheet night pads (Whisper Bindazzz Night XXXL, Carmesi Air Feel Night XXXL+ 16s at ₹329) now carry the premium claim instead of thinness.

Biodegradable bamboo / corn-starch pads have moved from pure D2C to mainstream shelves (Saathi 12s from ₹360, Niine Bio, Carmesi compostable wrap) at roughly 2-3x mass price — and for a closed township the argument is disposal load, not eco-branding.

Cramp relief became a real sub-category rather than an accessory: stick-on 12-hour heat patches and roll-ons (Pee Safe Cramp Relief Roll On ₹169, Sirona/Nua Cramp Comfort) now get their own shelf space, and none of them need a drug licence.

Femcare brands have broadened into whole intimate-and-grooming baskets — Pee Safe, Carmesi, Sanfe and Azah now sell toilet-seat sanitizer, deodorant roll-ons, wipes, razors, pimple patches and trimmers under the same brand, so the category is no longer just a pad shelf.

Cycle-health and PCOS regimens went mainstream in nutraceutical form (Gynoveda selling ₹1,313-2,250 ayurvedic courses direct, plus myo-inositol and iron-folic positioned as femcare rather than pharma).

Quick-commerce normalised the emergency single-pack purchase in 10 minutes — a campus store's equivalent is a 24x7 hostel-block vending machine plus a discreet WhatsApp order-and-collect line, which is how you actually compete with the habit students bring from home.

Menstrual cups have settled rather than surged — ₹289-499 with sterilizer bundles doing the converting (Pee Safe cup ₹289, cup+sterilizer ₹399, Saathi ₹499) — while menstrual discs take over as the new premium format.

Nil GST on sanitary napkins (HSN 9619, since 2018) plus Jan Aushadhi 'Suvidha' pads at about ₹1/pad means the entire ₹1-to-₹30-per-pad spread on shelf is positioning and margin, not tax — so a value tier can be priced kindly and still out-earn the national brand.
adjacentServices: Sanitary-napkin vending machines in every girls' hostel block and the university hostels — coin/token or free-issue; this is the 10-minute-delivery equivalent for a campus and it fixes the 2am and Sunday-closed problem that currently sends nobody anywhere.

Electric pad incinerators plus opaque disposal bins per hostel floor, sold or leased with a consumables contract — a closed township must destroy its own femcare waste, and this is standard MHM practice for Indian residential schools.

Monthly institutional auto-issue: a standing case-rate order to Akal Academy hostels and Eternal University hostels against the academic calendar, so the store buys to a known number instead of guessing, and stockouts stop being possible.

Trust-funded free or subsidised pad issue for school girls, with a pre-assembled menarche kit handed over by the warden or school nurse at a girl's first period — highest-impact, lowest-cost programme in this lane.

Discreet order-and-collect over WhatsApp with brown-paper packing and a named pickup slot — the mechanism that lets a shy 12-year-old, or a staff woman buying a pregnancy test in a small community, transact without a public conversation.

A female-staffed femcare counter (or the femcare shelf sited inside the clothing store rather than the main POS queue) — in a conservative institutional setting, who is at the till decides whether the category sells at all.

Menstrual-health education sessions with the campus nurse or a female counsellor, including menstrual-cup fitting and hygiene counselling — cups and cloth pads do not convert on a shelf, only after a demo.

A covered, heated drying line or drying room for reusable cloth pads and period underwear — without it the monsoon makes the reusable tier unhygienic, and the reusable tier is exactly what a 50-km-from-market township should want.

Pregnancy-test and UTI referral pathway into the campus dispensary, so the store sells the OTC tier legally and hands off anything needing a pharmacist or a doctor instead of stocking Schedule H drugs.
Cup/cloth-pad sterilising point (kettle or steriliser container loan) near the hostel washrooms, removing the 'boil it in a shared kitchen' barrier that kills reusable adoption.
